reason: I want to prepare the flight carrier to keep the discovery cold during transfer; fitting it with reconditioned packs seems useful first.
expectation: The cold packs will provide the carrier with a temporary cooling margin, though it may still need an active power connection.

alternatives.reason: Placing the discovery case on the transfer bench also advances the transfer, but I want the receiving carrier prepared first.

effect: The flight carrier is now conditioned, so I can prepare the transfer at the cold bench.
reaction: The result is straightforward; I am curious how the transfer will keep the core cold.
reason: The discovery case needs to be at the transfer bench, so I will position it there.
expectation: The case will be placed at the bench, ready for a later transfer to the conditioned carrier.

alternatives.reason: I could place the conditioned carrier first; both appear necessary, and the order is unclear.

effect: The discovery case is at the cold transfer bench, and the carrier can now be combined with it.
reaction: The next transfer is clear, though I am curious how the core stays cold during it.
reason: I want to move the discovery into the prepared flight carrier, and this combination is offered at the transfer bench.
expectation: The body-bearing ice and its surrounding layer will move into the conditioned carrier, with the cold packs providing a transfer margin.

effect: The sealed liner, body-bearing ice, and neighboring ice are now together in the flight carrier. The carrier still needs a connection to flight cooling.
reaction: It is satisfying that the surrounding ice moved with the body; I am ready to secure it in the lander.
reason: The refrigerated sample bay is the only available combination and should connect the packed core to flight cooling.
expectation: The carrier will be placed in the lander's refrigerated bay and kept cold for flight, though the result may reveal another required step.

effect: The carrier is locked into the lander's bay and connected to powered cooling, completing the transfer with the core and its neighboring ice preserved.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the cold packs bridge the transfer and the refrigerator take over.

mostWorthwhile.text: Transferring the sealed liner into the flight carrier was most worthwhile because the body and its untouched neighboring ice stayed together.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the case on the bench was a straightforward preparation with little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The transfer moved the entire sealed liner into the carrier, preserving the surrounding ice along with the body.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; each contributed to preparing, transferring, or cooling the core.

continue.text: I would continue to learn what Earth makes of the discovery, though this chapter's actions were mostly straightforward preparations.
